sentences.text: STXBP1-related disease is grouped in the Neurotransmitter release cycle research cluster.
STX1B-related disease shares mechanism evidence with STXBP1, and these genes are also linked in STRING.
VAMP2-related disease shares mechanism evidence with STXBP1, with both genes annotated to the Acetylcholine and Serotonin neurotransmitter release cycles.
SNAP25-related disease shares mechanism evidence with STXBP1, with both genes annotated to the Acetylcholine and Serotonin neurotransmitter release cycles.
The Natural History Study in Pediatric Patients with STXBP1 Encephalopathy with Epilepsy (NCT05462054) serves STXBP1-related disease.
The STXBP1 and SYNGAP1 Related Disorders Natural History Study (NCT06555965) also serves STXBP1-related disease.

Natural History Study in Pediatric Patients with STXBP1 Encephalopathy with Epilepsy covers 55% of STX1B-related disease phenotype terms (5 of 8 mapped), based on overlap of STX1B phenotypes with study seizure endpoints and STX1B–STXBP1 mechanism linkage.
Asociación Síndrome STXBP1 (Spain) supports the STXBP1 community.
The European STXBP1 Consortium (ESCO) supports STXBP1-related disorders.
The Raging Raymond Foundation focuses on VAMP2-related disease, a mechanism-sharing neighbor of STXBP1.

sentences.text: GNAO1-related disease looks clinically similar to STXBP1-related disease in our data but is not supported as sharing mechanism, so it is excluded from current cross-disease leverage.
CACNA1A-related disease overlaps only by a single shared process term (Regulation of insulin secretion), which is weak for mechanism sharing and needs caution.
SLC2A1-related disease overlaps only by a single shared process term (Regulation of insulin secretion), which is weak for mechanism sharing and needs caution.
GRIN1-related disease overlaps only by a single shared process term (Neurexins and neuroligins), which is weak for mechanism sharing and needs caution.
Variant evidence differs against CACNA1A-related disease: STXBP1 has loss-of-function evidence, while CACNA1A includes gain-of-function evidence.
Variant evidence differs against GRIN1-related disease: STXBP1 has loss-of-function evidence, while GRIN1 includes gain-of-function evidence.
Contradictory genotype–phenotype evidence is indexed: no correlation between seizure severity and ID severity in STXBP1-related disease.
Contradictory genotype–phenotype evidence is indexed: no correlation between mutation type and seizure characteristics or cognitive outcome in STXBP1-related disease.
Contradictory genotype–phenotype evidence is indexed: recurrent variants were not associated with distinct electroclinical syndromes or overall clinical similarity in STXBP1-related disease.
Rikke S Møller has published on both STXBP1- and STX1B-related disease.
Ingo Helbig has published on STXBP1-related disease and leads related research efforts.

Review the Natural History Study in Pediatric Patients with STXBP1 Encephalopathy with Epilepsy for coverage of STX1B-related disease phenotypes (target: 0.55, 5/8 terms) and verify Rikke S Møller as a contact for STX1B–STXBP1 linkage.

## Who shares our characteristics
STXBP1-related disease is grouped in the Neurotransmitter release cycle research cluster. [8b8a74101835d1d2]
STX1B-related disease shares mechanism evidence with STXBP1, and these genes are also linked in STRING. [ab5fe5ff268d13ba, 8a5b259c2af7cfea]
VAMP2-related disease shares mechanism evidence with STXBP1, with both genes annotated to the Acetylcholine and Serotonin neurotransmitter release cycles. [ca33d6f8f475990e, cdc0a9af79e4b2f6, 78d613b03a5d2f16, e6d5b0914532b438, d8497858c88a7d26]
SNAP25-related disease shares mechanism evidence with STXBP1, with both genes annotated to the Acetylcholine and Serotonin neurotransmitter release cycles. [fcb938d1b0386f7c, cdc0a9af79e4b2f6, 78d613b03a5d2f16, c8fcfc6ef79c0a33, 9c42c5bf01870c1c]

## What already exists
The Natural History Study in Pediatric Patients with STXBP1 Encephalopathy with Epilepsy (NCT05462054) serves STXBP1-related disease. [bc71e274e1c691ec]
The STXBP1 and SYNGAP1 Related Disorders Natural History Study (NCT06555965) also serves STXBP1-related disease. [dcec503694916ae3]
Natural History Study in Pediatric Patients with STXBP1 Encephalopathy with Epilepsy covers 55% of STX1B-related disease phenotype terms (5 of 8 mapped), based on overlap of STX1B phenotypes with study seizure endpoints and STX1B–STXBP1 mechanism linkage. [bc71e274e1c691ec, 3c0ab7caccfc6cb4, 3ddef56861713c92, 4e5e828ba255e763, 4a4f52c38a51ab40, ab5fe5ff268d13ba]
Asociación Síndrome STXBP1 (Spain) supports the STXBP1 community. [453d4be996145f4e]
The European STXBP1 Consortium (ESCO) supports STXBP1-related disorders. [ba44da54694ec39f]
The Raging Raymond Foundation focuses on VAMP2-related disease, a mechanism-sharing neighbor of STXBP1. [202ca5201eca2102, ca33d6f8f475990e]

## What differs and must be verified
GNAO1-related disease looks clinically similar to STXBP1-related disease in our data but is not supported as sharing mechanism, so it is excluded from current cross-disease leverage. [f94ad5494a3e9ab8]
CACNA1A-related disease overlaps only by a single shared process term (Regulation of insulin secretion), which is weak for mechanism sharing and needs caution. [34c9bc447921f8cb, 3a40a3f53a18b664, 187be2699f417de6]
SLC2A1-related disease overlaps only by a single shared process term (Regulation of insulin secretion), which is weak for mechanism sharing and needs caution. [20c30f77dc2491fb, 3a40a3f53a18b664, 5490966f0991bdf8]
GRIN1-related disease overlaps only by a single shared process term (Neurexins and neuroligins), which is weak for mechanism sharing and needs caution. [9b5a310872598764, ce6dd3aad07a277e, 072a91fd2fdb335f]
Variant evidence differs against CACNA1A-related disease: STXBP1 has loss-of-function evidence, while CACNA1A includes gain-of-function evidence. [87257c69fcfbcdad, df57b34e24ef5206, 4e69b8ecbf6740e9, c3ec464ea6412040]
Variant evidence differs against GRIN1-related disease: STXBP1 has loss-of-function evidence, while GRIN1 includes gain-of-function evidence. [87257c69fcfbcdad, df57b34e24ef5206, c9e703902a0fb3f5, 0211d2b50f1f9730]
Contradictory genotype–phenotype evidence is indexed: no correlation between seizure severity and ID severity in STXBP1-related disease. [b1f9e5eeafbc81d2]
Contradictory genotype–phenotype evidence is indexed: no correlation between mutation type and seizure characteristics or cognitive outcome in STXBP1-related disease. [e362983ef11a54b1]
Contradictory genotype–phenotype evidence is indexed: recurrent variants were not associated with distinct electroclinical syndromes or overall clinical similarity in STXBP1-related disease. [ddc8cd6784a496fb]

## Who to contact
Rikke S Møller has published on both STXBP1- and STX1B-related disease. [00ad11fdd61a5e6f, 2eea3ae9e8a1455e, 4e3da81614f6d08d]
Ingo Helbig has published on STXBP1-related disease and leads related research efforts. [0bead7fade435d02, 18e9e45f700b90dd, 220ad6798167d0d5]

## Proposed first joint step
Review the Natural History Study in Pediatric Patients with STXBP1 Encephalopathy with Epilepsy for coverage of STX1B-related disease phenotypes (target: 0.55, 5/8 terms) and verify Rikke S Møller as a contact for STX1B–STXBP1 linkage.
